title: Hibiscus Ice Pops
changes_from_base: A sweetened hibiscus infusion with lime replaces the strawberry purée.
summary: Deep red, tart hibiscus ice pops lifted with a touch of lime.
equipment: ice-pop bags or eight 120 ml moulds and sticks

ingredients.item: key lime juice (or 1 tbsp ordinary lime juice)
fine sea salt or table salt

steps.title: Boil
steps.text: Bring 40 g dried hibiscus flowers and 945 ml cold water to the boil, then simmer for 10 min and cool for 30-60 min.

steps.title: Strain
steps.text: Strain the liquid into a jug.

steps.title: Whisk
steps.text: Whisk in 230 g caster sugar, 2 tbsp key lime juice and a pinch of salt until the sugar dissolves.

steps.title: Fill
steps.text: Fill ice-pop bags about a third full, around 115 g each, and tie leaving room to expand, or fill the moulds.

tips: Simmer the hibiscus flowers for the full 10 min to draw out as much colour and flavour as possible.
Leave room in the bags before tying, since the liquid expands as it freezes.
The strained hibiscus flowers can be kept and used again in another drink or dish.
storage: Keep the pops in their bags or moulds in the freezer.
